title: XRootD Storage Activity
description: What the monitored XRootD servers are doing, aggregated by xrdmoncollect: throughput and file operations, sessions, errors, redirects and the g-stream backends. Per-user, per-VO and per-dataset detail lives only in the documents -- see the Loki dashboards. The collector's own health is in grafana-collector-dashboard.json.

panels.title: Read
panels.description: Bytes read from the cluster per second.

panels.title: Write
panels.description: Bytes written to the cluster per second.

panels.title: Open files
panels.description: Files currently open across the cluster.

panels.title: Open sessions
panels.description: Client sessions currently connected. Counted from the user dictionary, so it stays at zero unless the servers' monitor directive includes a "user" destination.

panels.title: Operations/s
panels.description: File operations reported by the servers.

panels.title: Error rate
panels.description: Operations that concluded unsuccessfully, as a share of all reported operations.

panels.title: Sessions/s
panels.description: Client sessions ending per second.

panels.title: Servers
panels.description: Servers reporting for the selected clusters.

panels.title: Throughput by direction
panels.description: Bytes moved, from the fstat "xfr" block. Unlike the read/readv/write counts below, this needs no "ops" in the servers' fstat directive.

panels.title: File operations/s
panels.description: Opens and closes are always reported; the read, readv and write counts come from the fstat "ops" block and stay flat at zero unless the servers are configured to send it.

panels.title: Top servers by throughput
panels.description: The ten busiest servers, which is how an unbalanced cluster shows itself.

panels.title: Open files and sessions
panels.description: Live per-server occupancy.

panels.title: Throughput by application
panels.description: The ten heaviest client applications, named by the i-stream appid when the client sends one and by the login executable otherwise. This series carries no server label, so it is not narrowed by the Server variable.

panels.title: Volume by application and direction
panels.description: Totalled over the dashboard window. An application that only ever appears under readv is doing vectored reads, which is usually analysis rather than staging.

panels.title: Sessions ended/s
panels.description: Client disconnects per server.

panels.title: Session duration
panels.description: Wall-clock time clients stay connected. The histogram is kept per cluster, not per server, so the Server variable does not narrow it.

panels.title: Session start resolution
panels.description: How each session's start time was established. login and connect are exact; first_activity is inferred from the first record seen, and disconnect means nothing was known and the duration is reported as zero. A rising disconnect share means session durations above are understated -- usually the servers are not sending the u (user) stream.

panels.title: Failed operations/s by category
panels.description: Operations that concluded unsuccessfully, from the close record's error trailer and from standalone f-stream error records.

panels.title: Error ratio by server
panels.description: Failures as a share of that server's reported operations, which isolates one sick node from a cluster-wide problem.

panels.title: Redirects/s by kind
panels.description: Client redirects issued by the server. Needs redir in the servers' xrootd.monitor directive.

panels.title: HTTP requests/s
panels.description: From the http g-stream provider, broken down by method and response status.

panels.title: HTTP error ratio
panels.description: Client and server error responses as a share of all HTTP requests.

panels.title: Third-party copies/s
panels.description: Completed TPC transfers by type and outcome. The type comes verbatim from the record and is reported as unknown when the plugin does not set it.

panels.title: TPC throughput
panels.description: Bytes moved by third-party copy.

panels.title: TPC size distribution
panels.description: How large third-party copies are, from the tpc_size_bytes histogram. A population that has shifted into the smallest bucket usually means transfers are failing early rather than that the files got smaller.

panels.title: Proxy cache (PFC)
panels.description: File closes and bytes served by the proxy file cache, by where the data came from.

panels.title: Proxy cache hit ratio
panels.description: Bytes served from cache as a share of hit plus miss. Bypass and prefetch are excluded: bypass never consults the cache, and prefetch is fill traffic rather than a client read.

panels.title: OSS ops/s (with slow)
panels.description: Storage-system calls from the oss g-stream provider, and how many of them the plugin classified as slow.

panels.title: Throttle plugin
panels.description: I/O the throttle plugin handled, and how much of it is in flight. A rising in-flight count with a flat rate means clients are being held.

panels.title: FRM stage / purge
panels.description: File residency manager activity from the x and p streams: staging transfers, purge events, and the space purging reclaimed.
